ruling.recommended_action: Record the unexcused route deviation in the driver's file and send the driver's account to Ryde account review for a repeated route breach (this is the 3rd upheld route dispute in 90 days); notify the rider that the fixed RydeX quote yields no cash refund.
ruling.reasoning:
The fare element is settled and not in dispute in the end. F6 shows a RydeX fixed quote of $24.93 built from base $3.90 + distance $15.06 (10.68 km) + time $4.50 + platform $1.47, with waiting $0.00, and F4 shows the billed 10.7 km does not exceed the 10.7 km optimal route [F4][F6][RD-2]. Because RydeX is non-metered, the extra kilometres driven do not enter the fare, so the refundable amount is $0 and the money outcome is no_action [F4][F5][RD-2][FARE-1]. Amount is null because no refund is computed from any gps or fare value.

The deviation itself is real and unexcused. F1 (+4.5 km, +42%) and F3 (14:19–14:26, 5.03 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, adding 3.64 km, up to 1160 m off route) establish one off-route segment well above data-layer noise, which the driver does not contest [F1][F3][RD-1]. No traffic excuse exists: F11 records no incident near the route and F9/F10 are only LTA speed band 4 (30–39 km/h), outside the band 1–2 corroboration the clause recognises, so RD-4(a) fails and RD-4(b) cannot exempt on its own [F9][F10][F11][RD-4]. F12 (fair, 0.0 mm rain) removes weather as a cause [F12][RD-4].

On consent, the chat record is empty — F7 shows no in-app messages at all — so there is no rider message timestamped before the segment start of 14:19 that agrees to any route; F8 is the driver's own post-trip statement ("The GPS rerouted me") and a driver's claim of agreement is not consent [F7][F8][RD-5]. The segment therefore counts as an unexcused route deviation, grounding a recorded RD-1 breach [F3][RD-1][RD-2]. RD-3(a) does not apply: no stop was measured and no rider message named any place [F3][RD-3].

RD-6 attaches because a breach is recorded and the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2, i.e. a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days, making this a repeated breach [F14][RD-6]. This drives the account-review referral only; the profile fact is not used to establish the deviation itself [F14][RD-6]. The safety screen is clean: F7 contains no messages and neither F8 nor the complaint contains any threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation arises [F7][F8][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

segment_findings.reason: F7 shows the chat record contains no in-app messages at all, so there is no rider message sent before the 14:19 segment start agreeing to this route, and F8 is the driver's post-trip statement ('The GPS rerouted me'), which is not rider consent [F7][F8][RD-5]. No RD-3(a) stop was measured and no place was named by the rider [F3][RD-3]. The 3.64 km extra at F3 is therefore an unexcused deviation [F3][RD-1].

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted in part: the fare arithmetic is right (F4, F6 show no toll, no waiting fee and no add-on), but the claim that nothing is in dispute is wrong as to the breach point — an unexcused segment still grounds a recorded RD-1 violation even when the refund computes to $0 [F3][F4][F6][RD-1][RD-2].

Granted: the unexcused deviation at F3 is recorded as an RD-1 breach, but the only money consequence under RD-2 on a fixed-quote RydeX fare is $0, so the case closes no_action rather than with a refund [F1][F3][F4][RD-1][RD-2].

Granted as to the flag: F14's 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days plus this recorded breach make RD-6's 'repeated' condition apply, but the profile fact is used only as the basis for the additional account action, not to establish the deviation [F3][F14][RD-6].

Rejected: an empty chat at F7 is not permission — RD-5 requires a rider message before the segment, and the absence of any message means there is no consent, not that none was needed; F8 is a post-trip statement and is not consent [F3][F7][F8][RD-5].

Rejected: RD-4 requires a traffic incident on the replaced optimal stretch (F11 records none), and the band 4 readings at F9/F10 are outside the band 1–2 corroboration and cannot exempt a segment alone; the reroute is unexcused congestion speculation, not a policy excuse [F3][F9][F10][F11][F12][RD-4].

Accepted on the consequence but not on the framing: RD-6 does attach the account-review flag given the prior at F14 and the recorded breach at F3, and RD-2 fixes the cash remedy at $0 on this fixed fare [F3][F4][F14][RD-2][RD-6].
